newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FUN IN BRUSSELS - THE BEST OF DUTCH MODERN ART.
newsitem.headline: FUN IN BRUSSELS - THE BEST OF DUTCH MODERN ART.

text.p: In Brussels to attend a meeting of the veterinary committee or to try to influence draft legislation on insurance brokers? Within a stone's throw of the European district there is a unique opportunity to admire the finest paintings from five Dutch museums.

"The Art of Collecting" exhibition at the Palais des Beaux-Arts is showing work by 12 leading Dutch 20th century artists -- including Jan Schoonhoven, Charley Toorop and Piet Mondrian -- along with work by international artists who were active in the same period, and it illustrates how Dutch artworks fit in with international trends.

The exhibition's poster features Picasso's "Seated woman with fish hat", but don't be fooled into thinking that it is an exhibition all about international art in Dutch museums, although there are works by Georges Braque, Marc Chagall and Picasso.

Chagall's poetic "Tribute to Apollinaire" stands next to transparent and ambiguous works by Rene Daniels and German expressionist Karl Schmidt-Rottluff, while Picasso is also associated with some fine sculptures by Karel Appel and paintings by Constant, which belonged to the Cobra movement.

The exhibition's main attraction is that it gathers under one roof some 150 paintings and sculptures otherwise dispersed through the five participating museums in Amsterdam, The Hague, Eindhoven, Rotterdam and Otterlo.
PRACTICAL: Palais des Beaux-Arts, Rue Royale 10, Brussels. The exhibition, which runs until May 25, is open daily except Mondays from 1000 to 1800. Entrance fee is 250 Belgian francs.
